## Exact input and cost contract

Let M=2^d. The known, succinctly indexed state set is

    {A, B} union {u_j, v_j : j in {0,1}^d}.

The endpoints A and B are supplied. The generator has the following nonzero off-diagonal rates:

    q(A,u_j) = q(B,v_j) = 1/M,
    q(u_j,A) = q(v_j,B) = 1,
    q(u_j,v_j) = q(v_j,u_j) = theta_j.

All other off-diagonal rates are zero. Diagonal rates are minus the row sum. The unknown theta_j are positive rational numbers.

The learner receives all of this structure, M, and the complete stationary law. It may query theta_j at *any* chosen index, adaptively, at unit cost. This query reveals the entire unknown local generator row at u_j and v_j. Exact samples of the known stationary law are free. Known endpoint transitions can be sampled or evaluated freely. Listing all M endpoint successors costs M outputs; it does not reveal any theta_j. Random bits and arithmetic may be free for the lower bound.

This is at least as informative as microscopic dynamics that must inspect a local rate before evolving there. The lower bound charges gate inspections, rather than the enormous physical waiting time. It is not a lower bound against additional symbolic input that identifies the special gate or certifies a restricted response class.

## Theorem 1: all models have exactly the same equilibrium

For every positive theta vector, the chain is irreducible and reversible with

    pi(A)=pi(B)=1/4,
    pi(u_j)=pi(v_j)=1/(4M).

Proof: these masses sum to one. On A--u_j, both directed equilibrium flows equal 1/(4M); likewise on B--v_j. On u_j--v_j, both equal theta_j/(4M). Thus detailed balance holds edge by edge. In particular, neither equilibrium samples nor equilibrium thermodynamic observables identify the kinetic gates.

## Theorem 2: exact committor, capacity, route law, and mean first-passage time

Define f(theta)=theta/(1+2theta) and S=sum_j f(theta_j). Then

    h(u_j)=f(theta_j),
    h(v_j)=(1+theta_j)/(1+2theta_j),
    cap(A,B)=S/(4M),
    P(reactive channel=j)=f(theta_j)/S,
    E_A[tau_B]=2M/S.

Here h(x)=P_x(tau_B<tau_A), with h(A)=0 and h(B)=1. Capacity means the stationary A-to-B reactive flux. The channel means the corridor used by a successful A-to-B excursion; it is not a geometric-path approximation.

Proof of the committor: on corridor j, the harmonic equations are

    (1+theta) h(u) = theta h(v),
    (1+theta) h(v) = 1+thet

\section{Rare-event acquisition: exact kinetics can remain hidden}

The proposed scientific-computing capability was trustworthy pathway and rate
acceleration without a supplied route, committor or transition-state map.
Automatic basin boosts overlap
\href{https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.3908}{Voter's hyperdynamics};
corrected learned proposals already occur in FlowRES. The missing general
operation is not another proposal density, but acquisition of an important
unseen kinetic gate. The following finite-state construction makes that boundary
exact. It is not a universal lower bound on atomistic simulation.

\subsection{Exact oracle contract and construction}

Let $M=2^d$, with known states $A,B,u_j,v_j$ for $j\in\{0,1\}^d$.
The nonzero off-diagonal rates are
\[
 q(A,u_j)=q(B,v_j)=1/M,\quad q(u_j,A)=q(v_j,B)=1,\quad
 q(u_j,v_j)=q(v_j,u_j)=\theta_j>0.
\]
Diagonals make row sums zero. Topology, endpoints and all displayed known
rates are supplied. An adaptive query at any chosen $j$ reveals exact
$\theta_j$, hence both unknown local rows, at unit cost.
Exact sampling of the known equilibrium is free. Arithmetic and randomness
may even be free for the lower bound. Listing $M$ successors costs $M$ outputs
and reveals no $\theta_j$.

Detailed balance gives the same law for every parameter vector:
\[
 \pi(A)=\pi(B)=1/4,\qquad \pi(u_j)=\pi(v_j)=1/(4M).
\]
Write $f(x)=x/(1+2x)$ and $S=\sum_j f(\theta_j)$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact route and clock]\label{thm:corridor}
The committor with boundary values $h(A)=0,h(B)=1$, stationary reactive flux,
successful-excursion route law and mean passage time are
\[
 h(u_j)=f(\theta_j),\quad
 h(v_j)=\frac{1+\theta_j}{1+2\theta_j},\quad
 \operatorname{cap}(A,B)=\frac{S}{4M},\quad
 w_j=\frac{f(\theta_j)}{S},\quad \E_A\tau_B=\frac{2M}{S}.
\]
For $s\ge0$, writing
$b(s)=M^{-1}\sum_j\theta_j/(s+1+2\theta_j)$,
\[
 \E_Ae^{-s\tau_B}=\frac{b(s)}{s(s+2)+b(s)}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The two interior harmonic equations are
$(1+\theta)h(u)=\theta h(v)$ and
$(1+\theta)h(v)=1+\theta h(u)$; solve them and sum equilibrium successful
fluxes from $A$ to get the capacity and route law.
Each attempt consists of an $A$ holding time of mean one and an interior
excursion of mean one: the total exit hazard from $\{u_j,v_j\}$ to
$\{A,B\}$ is identically one. Its success probability averaged over the
uniformly chosen corridor is $S/M$. Renewal

The rational solver does not use the proposed closed-form hitting-time formula.
No sampled trajectories, atomistic force field, or physical validation are used.

from fractions import Fraction as F

def solve(a, b):
    a = [list(row) + [value] for row, value in zip(a, b)]
    n = len(b)
    for k in range(n):
        pivot = next(i for i in range(k, n) if a[i][k])
        a[k], a[pivot] = a[pivot], a[k]
        scale = a[k][k]
        a[k] = [x / scale for x in a[k]]
        for i in range(n):
            if i != k and a[i][k]:
                scale = a[i][k]
                a[i] = [x - scale * y for x, y in zip(a[i], a[k])]
    return [row[-1] for row in a]

    m = len(theta)
    n = 2 * m + 2
    q = [[F(0) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]

        q[0][u] = q[1][v] = F(1, m)
        q[u][0] = q[v][1] = F(1)
        q[u][v] = q[v][u] = t
    for i in range(n):
        q[i][i] = -sum(q[i])
    return q
